summary: Fujio Oda is a history and archaeology scholar who studied at Kyushu University (~1953–1957). He held posts at Beppu University (~1962–1986) and Fukuoka University (~1986–2004).

Fujio Taniguchi specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He earned his PhD at Nagoya University under Musashi Tachikawa and studied under several teachers including Yusho Miyasaka. He was attested at the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute in 2026.

Fumi Yao works in Buddhist studies and Indology. Attested in 2026, Yao holds posts as an associate professor at the University of Tokyo and as a part-time lecturer at the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute and Taisho University.

Fumihiko Sueki specializes in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Yoshiro Tamura, Kyosho Hayashima, and Hajime Nakamura, later serving as professor at Tokyo (1995–2009) and the International Research Center for Japanese Studies (~2009–2015).

Fumihiro Okada specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. Okada studied at the University of Tokyo (attested 2015) and held a post as a specially appointed associate professor at Minobusan University (attested 2026).

Fumimaro Watanabe (1934–1990) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Ryukoku University and the University of Toronto under A. K. Warder and Hammalawa Saddhatissa. He held professorships at Kindai University (1981) and Aichi Gakuin University (1987).

Fumimasa Fukui (1934–2017) was a Buddhist studies and sinology scholar. He studied at Waseda University and the École Pratique des Hautes Études under Paul Demiéville, Max Kaltenmark, and Rolf Alfred Stein. He served as a professor at Waseda University (~1978–2005).
Fumio Enomoto works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He served as a research assistant at Kyoto University (~1980–1984) and as a professor at Osaka University (~1999–2017).

Fumio Masutani (1902–1987) was a Buddhist and religious studies scholar educated at the University of Tokyo. He held professorships at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (~1954–1966) and Taisho University (~1966–1973), and served as president of Tsuru University (1969–1971).

Fumio Ouchi specializes in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and sinology. He completed his doctoral studies at Otani University, where he served as associate professor (~1993–2000) and professor (~2000–2017).

Fumio Shoji is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Rissho University. He served there as an assistant professor in the Faculty of Buddhist Studies (~2014–2017) and became an associate professor in ~2017.
Fumio Tamamuro is a scholar of Japanology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Meiji University (~1956–1966) and subsequently held a post there (~1968–2006).
Fung Kei Cheng works in Buddhist and religious studies. Cheng earned a PhD at the University of Hong Kong under the supervision of Samson Tse (attested 2014).
Futoshi Omae is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He held posts as a lecturer at Kyushu University (attested 1986–1991) and at Shimane Prefectural Junior College (attested 1997).

Futoshi Takehashi specializes in Buddhist studies. He pursued doctoral studies at Otani University (attested 1992) and served as an assistant at the Shinshu Otani-ha Institute of Shin Buddhist Studies (1995–1997).
Fuyuan Luo is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. Luo is attested in 2026 as a PhD student at the University of Cambridge studying under Adam Yuet Chau.

Fyodor Buslaev (1818–1897) was a linguist, historian, and archaeologist. He studied at the Faculty of History and Philology of Moscow University (~1834–1838) and held a post at Moscow State University beginning in 1846.

Fyodor Shcherbatskoy (1866–1942) was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Saint Petersburg State University and under Georg Bühler and Hermann Jacobi. He served as professor at Saint Petersburg State University (~1909–1941) and founded the Institute of Buddhist Culture.

Félix Nève (1816–1893) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He earned his doctorate at KU Leuven (~1834–1838) and studied under Christian Lassen, Friedrich Wilhelm Thiersch, and Eugène Burnouf. He was appointed professor at KU Leuven in 1841.

G. B. Palsule (1920–2007) worked in Indology and linguistics. He held posts at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute as a sub-editor in the Dictionary Department (attested 1957) and at Savitribai Phule Pune University (attested 1987).
